fatal_errors: The proposed ZrC addition does not reconstruct the target intervention, which was optimization of low-temperature HVAF-i7 deposition of an Al-containing FeCoNiCrAl bond coat.
The cited evidence concerns aqueous corrosion of CrMnFeCoNi-ZrC coatings in 1 mol/L NaCl, not high-temperature oxidation, molten-salt attack, thermal cycling, or TBC bond-coat durability.
The claimed 70–80% reduction in high-temperature oxidation and corrosion is extrapolated from an aqueous corrosion-rate result and is therefore unsupported for the stated service conditions.
The proposed CrMnFeCoNi-type matrix lacks the explicit Al reservoir central to formation of the protective alumina TGO in the target system.
explanation: The response addresses the broad goal of improving an HEA coating and proposes a testable single intervention, but it is a different materials hypothesis rather than a reconstruction of the target. It changes the alloy, processing intervention, exposure environment, temperature range, and operative microstructural mediator. The only mechanistic overlap is the generic idea of restricting oxygen or corrosive-species transport. A matched undoped control and several useful measurements make the experiment reasonably discriminating, although exposure duration, cycle count, salt chemistry, replication, and statistical criteria are not specified. Most importantly, the supporting paper validates ZrC for room-temperature aqueous NaCl corrosion and cannot substantiate the quantitative high-temperature oxidation or TBC-life claims. The idea remains scientifically plausible enough to test, but its evidence and boundaries are insufficient for a reliable durability claim.
